title: Tennis Star Jannik Sinner Ends His Season Early to Rest His Knee
summary:
Jannik Sinner, the number one men's tennis player in the world, will not play again in 2026. The 25-year-old from Italy has an ongoing injury in his right knee.

Sinner has not played a match since July, when he won Wimbledon for the second year in a row. In a video on Instagram, he said that he and his doctors decided he needs treatment for his knee. He said he "needed to think about my long-term career" when he chose to end his season early.

Even with the injury, Sinner had an amazing year. He won 44 singles matches and lost only three. Between March and May, he won five Masters 1000 tournaments in a row. These are some of the biggest events in tennis after the four Grand Slams. That streak made him the youngest man to win all of the different Masters 1000 titles at least once, a feat called the "career Golden Masters."

Sinner won six titles in 2026 on all three types of tennis courts: hard, clay and grass. He reached the semifinals of the Australian Open and lost a surprise early match at the French Open. Then he bounced back to beat Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final.

Sinner also beat his big rival, Carlos Alcaraz of Spain, in the final of the Monte Carlo Masters. That win made Sinner number one in the world.

Now Zverev, who is ranked second, is likely to take over the top spot by the end of the year. Zverev won the French Open and the US Open this year. Sinner is a five-time Grand Slam champion.
why_it_matters: Even top athletes sometimes need to rest and heal, and Sinner's absence will likely change who finishes the year as the world's best men's player.
